hook: The site of Jonathan Kittredge's Carpenter Gothic house of 1855, under a hotel of 1908.

parcel.note: Business addresses are usually deferred on this site; this page exists because the prompting source locates its subject on this parcel. The parcel is a corner one and the datasets disagree about which frontage names it: the assessor's property_location says 140 Ellis Street, SF Parcels and SF Planning both say 138 Cyril Magnin Street, and EAS carries 124 Ellis, 140 Ellis and 138 Cyril Magnin. The page follows the assessor and the street the prompting source names; DBI files permits under 124 and 140 Ellis and 120, 138 and 150 Cyril Magnin.

present_use.name: Hotel Fusion
present_use.note: The hotel names 140 Ellis Street as its address, which is what ties the 1855 house the prompting source describes to this parcel.

historic_status.ceqa_status_label: Historical resource; within an Article 11 conservation district

permits.description: The basement restaurant renovated — new interior partitions and finishes, new structural openings in the existing roof and structural walls, and new plumbing and electrical work.
The aluminium storefront system replaced, and a steel and glass canopy added above the lobby entrance.
An interior remodel of 17,315 sq ft across the first basement and first floor, changing the use to include new assembly space.
Meeting, breakfast and fitness rooms built in vacant street-level space, with a new steel structure creating an additional storey between the first and second levels to carry hotel offices.
A new entrance on Ellis Street and a new sidewalk, a new stair from the ground floor to the basement, and a change of occupancy, with new walls, kitchen, restrooms and HVAC.
Unreinforced-masonry seismic retrofit of the hotel and its ground-floor retail, with accessibility work.

permit_summary.note: Seven of the 140 filings on this parcel are shown — the largest by stated cost, plus the earliest that carries a description. The rest are fire-alarm and sprinkler permits, sign and street-space permits, fee revisions to the permits above, and the filings DBI holds under the parcel's Cyril Magnin Street numbers. The earliest filing on file, from February 1983, has no description recorded.

historical_record.description: Jonathan Kittredge, owner of the Phoenix Iron Works, built a two-and-a-half-storey gabled Carpenter Gothic house on the north side of Ellis Street between Powell and Mason for his Christmas Eve marriage. The homestead included an artesian well, a small backyard orchard and a cow.
